title: Slow up, fast down
hook: Slow up the hill, fast back down. What was your average speed?

doesNotKnow: that an average speed weighs each speed by the time spent at it

misconception: 30 km/h up and 60 km/h down average 45 km/h.
objective: The learner can explain that the round trip takes 2 h + 1 h, so 120 km in 3 h is 40 km/h: more time is spent at the slow speed, so it counts more.

claims.text: 60 km at 30 km/h takes 2 h; 60 km at 60 km/h takes 1 h.
claims.source: time = distance ÷ speed: 60/30 = 2, 60/60 = 1 (recomputed in node; hours() in Demo.tsx).

claims.text: Average speed is total distance ÷ total time: 120 km in 3 h is 40 km/h, not 45.
claims.source: Definition of average speed; 120/3 = 40 (node). Equivalent to the harmonic mean for equal distances: 2 × 30 × 60 / (30 + 60) = 40. avg() in Demo.tsx.

claims.text: On the chart each leg's block has width = hours and height = speed, so its area is the 60 km driven.
claims.source: speed × time = distance; 30 × 2 = 60 and v × 60/v = 60 for every slider value.

claims.text: 45 would be right only with equal time at each speed; with 2 hours at 30 and 1 at 60, (30 + 30 + 60) ÷ 3 = 40.
claims.source: Time-weighted mean: (30 × 2 + 60 × 1) / 3 = 40 (node). Equal times would give (30 + 60)/2 = 45.

recall.question: You cycle 10 km to work at 10 km/h and 10 km home at 20 km/h. Your average speed for the day's riding?
recall.why: 1 h there and 0.5 h back: 20 km in 1.5 h is about 13.3 km/h. You spend longer at the slow speed, so it counts more.
